items.title: Anthropic IPO 前三家机构如何重注押注
items.description: TechCrunch 报道 Notable Capital、GIC 和 Baillie Gifford 在 Anthropic IPO 前的重仓投资逻辑。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/dus34samsjrld1qopq65v54uq
items.excerpt:
How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
TechCrunch 报道 Notable Capital、GIC 和 Baillie Gifford 在 Anthropic IPO 前的重仓投资逻辑。
报道还原了 Notable Capital、GIC 和 Baillie Gifford 在 Anthropic 上市前的投资决策过程，可了解机构在争议时点押注的依据。
当Notable Capital把其10亿美元基金美国部分的约10%投入Anthropic的E轮融资时，许多有限合伙人（LP）对这笔巨额押注感到困惑。Claude的开发商当时仍落后于最大竞争对手OpenAI，而DeepSeek几周前刚发布R1模型，大有赶超闭源对手之势。此外，Anthropic估值高达615亿美元，是这家以早期投资为主的风投机构25年历史中投过的估值最高的公司。
但Notable的投资人看好Anthropic的未来。这家机构原名为GGV Capital，2024年与中国业务 分拆 。由管理合伙人Hans Tung（童士豪）、Glenn Solomon和投资经理Dan Cahana组成的团队分析数据后发现，开发者越来越偏爱Claude而非ChatGPT，使用Claude的时间占比达70%，与前一年相比出现逆转。
“我们很清楚，在AI领域，开发者处于核心位置，因为他们是早期采用者，”公司联合创始人童士豪对TechCrunch表示。
童士豪说，Notable亲身经历过中美关系的复杂局面，也因此确信“关键任务”类工作始终需要基于美国的闭源模型。
不到两年后，Notable的LP不再质疑这笔超常规的投资。周三，Anthropic在史上最大规模IPO中募资 813亿美元 ，次日股票开始交易前，完全稀释估值约为1.5万亿美元，账面回报约15倍。
当然，Notable并非唯一从Anthropic获得巨额账面收益的机构。即便是很少见到风投级回报倍数的传统后期投资者，也将收获颇丰。
新加坡主权财富基金GIC在整个2024年一直在研究Anthropic，但直到2025年初，该基金科技投资主管Chris Emanuel在旧金山意大利餐厅Che Fico与Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao会面后，才做出首笔投资。Rao展示了模型改进如何推动企业采用率上升，激发了Emanuel的兴趣。GIC随后在Anthropic的F轮融资中首次投资，该轮于2025年9月宣布，估值1830亿美元。
“Claude Code当时刚发布，”Emanuel对TechCrunch表示。“虽然还很早期，但即便那时我们也能看到它深受开发者欢迎的迹象。”GIC对这家AI实验室的信心极高，后来与Coatue共同领投了Anthropic估值3800亿美元的G轮融资，并在估值9650亿美元的IPO前轮次中再次作为联合领投方之一回归。据一位了解GIC财务情况的人士称，GIC在三轮融资中向Anthropic投资超过45亿美元，IPO后持股约相当于公司1%。
Baillie Gifford美国成长投资负责人Lilian Li在首次投资Anthropic的F轮之前，已研究该公司并与团队交流了近两年。Li对TechCrunch表示，当Baillie Gifford确信该公司在愿景上“持续稳定执行”，同时创造强劲营收和“可观的毛利率”后，便投资了这家Claude开发商。
Li说，Baillie Gifford首次投资后，Anthropic继续兑现承诺，拓展到法律服务和生命科学等行业，以及Cowork和网络安全等更广泛的应用领域。
她补充道：“他们的节奏一直跟得上变化的速度，这一点确实相当了不起。”贝利·吉福德随后在三轮融资中累计投入15亿美元，这笔押注为这家投资管理机构以及另外数十位投资方带来了可观的账面收益——这些投资方当初入股时的估值一度看似高得离谱。

Multiway Robotics showcased five autonomous material handling solutions at CeMAT Asia 2026 in Shanghai, including a wheeled humanoid robot designed for flexible industrial operations.
The exhibition, held from November 3 to 6, brought together logistics and automation companies demonstrating technologies for manufacturing, warehousing and internal material transportation.
Multiway’s lineup included its H01 wheeled humanoid, an omnidirectional sideloader, a narrow-aisle forklift, an autonomous pallet truck and a counterbalanced forklift for precision stacking.
The H01 wheeled humanoid robot combines a mobile base with two collaborative robotic arms, providing a combined payload capacity of up to 30 kg.
At the exhibition, the robot demonstrated tote handling, illustrating how mobile manipulation could support material handling tasks that require both movement and dexterity.
Unlike conventional autonomous mobile robots designed primarily for transportation, the H01 can manipulate objects using its dual-arm configuration.
Multiway says the design is intended for manufacturing and warehouse environments where handling requirements may change.
The company also presented four autonomous vehicles designed for different intralogistics operations.
Its MW-O15 omnidirectional sideloader is designed to transport long and heavy materials, with customizable payload configurations of up to 8,000 kg. Its multidirectional movement is intended to improve maneuverability in confined industrial spaces.
The MW-K16 autonomous very narrow aisle forklift targets high-density warehousing. It can operate in aisles as narrow as 1.75 meters and lift loads to heights of up to 16.5 meters.
A three-way fork mechanism allows the vehicle to handle pallets without turning within the aisle.
For pallet transportation, the MW-CT15 offers a rated payload of 1.5 tons and supports different pallet configurations. It is also designed for cross-floor transportation in multi-level facilities.
The MW-SE15 counterbalanced forklift focuses on precision stacking of material cages. According to Multiway, it supports stacking up to six levels, with a minimum single-side clearance of 10 mm and a maximum control error of 5 mm.

Anthropic has introduced Claude for Manufacturing , a new AI software offering designed to help manufacturers streamline everyday tasks, including preparing quotations, investigating quality problems, diagnosing equipment failures and managing supplier relationships.
Announced on November 12, the offering combines 17 manufacturing-specific skills with four software connectors, enabling Claude to work with information stored in systems already used by industrial companies.
The connectors support Autodesk Fusion, Infor, Microsoft 365 and Oracle NetSuite, bringing together engineering, operational, financial and administrative information.
Anthropic says the system is intended to reduce the time manufacturing professionals spend collecting and organizing information, while leaving important decisions and approvals to employees.
The company cites a 2025 Manufacturing Leadership Council survey in which 79 percent of manufacturers reported entering data manually.
Claude for Manufacturing includes skills covering sales, quality management, operations, supply chains, engineering design and equipment setup.
The software can carry out individual tasks or coordinate several stages of a process before presenting its findings for human review.
For example, when a manufacturer receives a request for quotation, an estimator can ask Claude to examine the customer’s requirements, identify missing information, compare costs from previous jobs and prepare a draft quotation.
Quality engineers can use the system to investigate failed inspections by reviewing previous reports, identifying possible causes and preparing corrective action documentation.
Maintenance technicians can provide sensor data, repair records, photographs and equipment manuals to help Claude identify potential causes of a breakdown.
The system can then rank possible explanations for the technician to investigate.
Other applications include preparing supplier requests, comparing quotations, generating engineering design variations and compiling production performance reports.
For plant managers, Claude can combine production figures into reports showing output against targets, equipment downtime and the financial consequences of lost production.
A central feature of the offering is its ability to retrieve information from established manufacturing and business software.

The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI has once again demonstrated the enormous cultural influence of video games. But while millions of players explore Rockstar Games’ latest virtual world, another form of technologically driven entertainment is preparing to enter the real-world sporting arena: humanoid robot fighting.
Released on November 19, GTA 6 is one of the gaming industry’s most prominent launches, highlighting the continuing popularity of interactive entertainment built around competition, action and increasingly sophisticated technology.
Could humanoid robot fighting eventually attract a comparable following, bringing elements of video gaming, combat sports and robotics together in a new spectator sport?
An Australian organization called the Humanoid Fighting Championship (HFC) is preparing to find out.
The championship’s inaugural event, HFC I, is scheduled for February 20, 2027, at Margaret Court Arena in Melbourne, following a postponement from its original November 21, 2026 date.
The competition will feature humanoid robots, including EngineAI T800 machines, fighting inside a purpose-built octagonal enclosure with protective shielding.
Unlike fully autonomous robots, the machines will be controlled live by human operators, combining the skills of the pilots with the physical capabilities of the robots.
The revised event format features 12 teams competing across six bouts in three categories.
Three Classic bouts will involve one-on-one contests between unarmed humanoid robots, while two Arsenal bouts will feature machines equipped with weapons.
The final contest, called Last Stand, will pit two machines against a single opponent whose identity has not yet been revealed.
Judges will assess damage and downtime, with teams permitted to repair their machines between rounds.
Robot fighting is not entirely new. Competitions involving remotely controlled machines have existed for decades, while China has already hosted humanoid robot sporting events and combat demonstrations.
However, the emergence of humanoid fighting leagues introduces a different dimension.
Rather than purpose-built wheeled fighting machines, the competitors resemble human athletes, with articulated limbs, sophisticated balance systems and increasingly capable motion control.

items.excerpt:
Global robotics investment is on course for a record year in 2026, with funding projected to reach $60.7 billion, although much of the growth is concentrated in a relatively small number of companies, according to a new report from venture capital firm F-Prime Capital .
The firm’s State of Robotics 2026 report, based on PitchBook data and its own analysis, suggests investment could approach the combined total of the previous four years.
Funding reached $22.1 billion in 2025, compared with $19.9 billion in 2024 and $13 billion in 2022.
However, the report highlights a widening gap between investor enthusiasm for robotics and the commercial performance of companies developing the technology.
According to F-Prime, robotics companies raised approximately $50.7 billion through September 2026, with most of the capital concentrated in unusually large funding rounds.
Of that total, $21.6 billion came from just 25 investments of $250 million or more, excluding the separate $16 billion Waymo and $5 billion Anduril transactions.
Together, these large investments accounted for approximately $42.6 billion, representing around 84 percent of the funding recorded during the period.
The report also identifies a strong geographical concentration, with approximately 80 percent of robotics investment going to companies in the Americas.
Investment in general-purpose robotics, including humanoid robots and robotics foundation models, has increased substantially.
F-Prime estimates that funding for this segment could reach $9.9 billion in 2026, compared with approximately $6.2 billion in 2025.
The report highlights major investments in companies developing humanoid robots, AI foundation models and technologies intended to improve robotic manipulation.
Autonomous vehicles remain a major destination for investment, with funding concentrated among a small number of companies developing robotaxis, autonomous trucks and related technologies.
F-Prime projects approximately $18.7 billion in autonomous vehicle investment for 2026, excluding Waymo’s $16 billion financing round.
Vertical robotics, covering applications such as manufacturing, logistics, defense, agriculture and construction, is projected to attract $25.2 billion.
The report identifies defense as a major contributor to investment growth, while manufacturing is also experiencing increased funding.

items.description: A single misplaced character can stop a business process. I was reminded of that recently when a WordPress workflow supporting Logistics Viewpoints stopped functioning. After working through the failure, I found an unexpected double quotation mark at the end of the first line of a PHP file involved in the process. Removing it restored the […] The post When One Character Stops the Workflow: The Hidden Digital Dependencies of Modern Supply Chains appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
A single misplaced character can stop a business process. I was reminded of that recently when a WordPress workflow supporting Logistics Viewpoints stopped functioning. After working through the failure, I found an unexpected double quotation mark at the end of the first line of a PHP file involved in the process. Removing it restored the workflow.
I had not deliberately edited the file, and I cannot establish how or when the character was introduced. A software update, hosting operation, automated process, inadvertent edit, or another cause is conceivable, but there is no evidence here to assign responsibility. Restoring the service solved the immediate problem. It did not establish its origin or guarantee that it could not happen again.
This was a small incident. Yet it exposed a dependence that is familiar to anyone running a modern supply chain: an otherwise useful system can become unavailable because one supporting component fails. The failure may occur far from the process that ultimately stops. For executives, the question is less whether individual applications are online than whether the business can still complete the work it depends on them to perform.
November 2026 offered several much larger reminders. On November 12, Microsoft 365 experienced a major disruption affecting Exchange Online and other services. In its preliminary incident findings , Microsoft described a defect introduced in July that interacted with increased traffic and reduced gateway capacity. More than 80 percent of the affected gateway servers were unresponsive at the low point. A latent software issue became a major outage when operating conditions changed.
The logistics consequences were not theoretical. On November 13, Maersk advised customers that emails, notifications, and updates might be delayed and directed urgent inquiries to local office telephone numbers. A company’s TMS need not fail for its logistics operation to be impaired. If an essential communications channel is unavailable, a shipment exception may still go unresolved.
On November 13, the Federal Aviation Administration imposed a nationwide ground stop after a telecommunications failure destabilized services supporting air traffic control. The stop lasted approximately four hours and 45 minutes. Schunk has renamed its humanoid robotics spin-off Tactilia Robotics , establishing a Munich-based company focused on developing modular robotic hands for industrial automation applications.

BlueBotics , a Swiss developer of autonomous navigation and fleet management technology, has updated its ANT locator system to enable companies to manage manual forklifts and autonomous mobile robots through a single platform.

The updated system includes an in-cab human-machine interface that allows forklift operators to indicate their availability and accept assignments directly.
ANT locator also provides continuous location data to ANT server, enabling coordination between manual forklifts and mobile robots operating in shared spaces.
According to BlueBotics, this can help prevent traffic congestion, reduce potential conflicts between vehicles and improve the use of warehouse space.
The system also supports pallet tracking by recording forklift positions during collection, transportation and delivery.
Additional analytics, including heatmaps and traffic information, allow warehouse operators to identify frequently used routes and potential inefficiencies.
ANT locator integrates with ANT server and can connect to existing warehouse management, manufacturing execution and enterprise resource planning systems.
BlueBotics says the unified approach can simplify software infrastructure, reduce licensing requirements and make mixed-fleet operations easier to manage.

The robot is designed to handle variations in towel positioning, fabric folds and gripping conditions without requiring an operator to supervise every movement.

Gobano says this recovery capability is essential for maintaining production without frequent human intervention.
Employees remain responsible for replenishing materials, maintenance and handling exceptions the robot cannot resolve.
The system uses Gobano’s Toutatis reinforcement learning engine, which combines human demonstrations, task-specific world models and experience gathered during operation.
Production data, including successful movements, failed grasps and recovery times, is used to identify opportunities for improving the robot’s performance.
Gobano reports daily throughput improvements of approximately 5 percent, although it has not provided detailed figures on the duration of that improvement rate.
The company says its approach prioritizes reliability before increasing operating speed, since faster movements offer limited benefits if they lead to more failures.
The laundry installation represents an early commercial application of Gobano’s technology, demonstrating how autonomous manipulation systems can perform repetitive industrial tasks involving flexible materials.
Gobano plans to extend operating periods, increase throughput and develop capabilities for handling additional materials and workflows.
The company also aims to transfer learning from existing installations to future robotic systems, reducing the time required to establish reliable autonomous operations.

items.title: Boston Dynamics gives Atlas wheels to test new reinforcement learning capabilities
items.description: Boston Dynamics has released a new video showing its Atlas humanoid robot performing a series of unusual maneuvers, including rolling on wheels, sliding sideways and executing a 360-degree jump. The demonstration is part of a research project exploring how reinforcement learning can improve robot movement, test actuator performance and strengthen the reliability of control systems […]
items.excerpt:
Boston Dynamics has released a new video showing its Atlas humanoid robot performing a series of unusual maneuvers, including rolling on wheels, sliding sideways and executing a 360-degree jump.
The demonstration is part of a research project exploring how reinforcement learning can improve robot movement, test actuator performance and strengthen the reliability of control systems under demanding conditions.
Engineers temporarily replaced Atlas’s feet with wheels, using custom adapters to attach commercially available scooter rims to the robot’s existing ankle actuators.
The modification allowed researchers to test the robot’s motors across a wide range of speeds and torque demands while evaluating how accurately behaviors learned in simulation could transfer to physical hardware.
Xiaoyu (Andy) Wu, a controls engineer at Boston Dynamics, explains: “A wheeled Atlas isn’t a product. It’s a research testbed.”
The project combines traditional motor control engineering with whole-body reinforcement learning, a technique that allows robots to develop movement strategies through repeated simulated training.
Boston Dynamics used millions of simulated scenarios to train Atlas before transferring the learned behaviors to the physical robot.
Some movements were developed using human motion capture recordings, including sliding maneuvers that the robot adapted to its wheeled configuration.
The 360-degree jump was generated using a trajectory-tracking policy based on a recording of a person performing the movement.
Wu says: “It was fascinating to see these little tricks emerge on their own. Give the policy wheels, and it figures out how to use them.”
The research also highlights the importance of accurately modeling motor characteristics during simulation.
If simulated actuators behave differently from their physical counterparts, robots may learn movements that cannot be reliably reproduced in real-world conditions.
Boston Dynamics says the findings are already being applied to Atlas’s standard configuration, with researchers working to improve its ability to respond to actuator failures and other unexpected operating conditions.
The ultimate objective is not to produce a wheeled version of Atlas, but to develop more robust control systems capable of supporting reliable humanoid robot operations in real-world environments.

用户实测记录了本地跑通 Mirobody 的完整流程，也包括扫描页漏读、LOINC 编码对不上和 2B 模型答错的细节，可作本地部署健康数据工作流的参考。
感谢这份详细的实测评测！💙 很高兴看到 MiniCPM5-2B 被用于本地优先的工作流。非常感谢你既分享了哪些地方好用，也分享了哪些地方可以改进！🙌
上个月的体检报告，我交给了开源项目 Mirobody，在自己 Mac 上从读报告到回答问题全跑通了，没填一个 API key。58 行化验数值逐项对过原件，全对。可第一次上传时，化验单那几页它一条都没读进来。
装法：Homebrew 装 llama.cpp 跑模型，colima 起 Docker 跑应用，设置页选「100% 在本机运行」，用默认的小模型 minicpm5-2b，读图交给 glm-ocr。模型下载加载 6 分钟。机器是 M4 Pro、48GB，模型走 Mac 的 GPU。
第一次传整份 14 页的 PDF，1 分钟处理完，进来 33 条，全是前几页的查体和结论，化验单 3 页一条没有。翻日志，读图的模型一次都没被调用。这 3 页是嵌在 PDF 里的扫描图，页眉页脚却是文字，按文档写的规则，有文字层的页不走 OCR。
我把这 3 页截成图片单独传，一分半处理完，58 行化验结果全进来了，数值和原件逐项对得上。错了 3 处小地方：红细胞的参考范围多读出一个「1」，一个项目名丢了个字，甘油三酯旁边印的上箭头没记下来。
Mirobody 主要干的事，是把每条读数对到标准编码 LOINC，不同医院、不同写法的同一项才能连成一条线。这 58 行对上了 20 行。生化、甲功、糖化基本都对上了，单位不同还会选不同的编码；血常规 22 项、尿常规 14 项一项没对上，卡在「白细胞WBC」这种中文直接连着缩写的写法上。
最有意思的是肌酐。报告上写的是「肌酐(Cre)」，而 Cre 在 LOINC 里查到的是一种耐药菌的培养检查。它判断这个名字有歧义，就留空，没有瞎猜。
然后我问它：「我这次体检有哪些指标超出了参考范围？」2B 小模型想了 84 秒，走了 11 步。报告上标了箭头的 5 项全找到了，但把一项在范围内的血糖也算成了超标。它查表没拿到数值，转头去翻了原文件，回答里的数字也没带来源链接。我的血脂和肝功能确实有几项偏高，具体数值就不放了。
接 Claude Code 这一步，我换成了项目自带的演示账号。MCP 接上以后，Claude Code 查到的读数会发到 Claude 的服务器，所以这一步没用我自己的数据。问它「胆固醇这几年怎么变的」，只有一条记录的时候，它直说看不出变化，没编趋势；我再传两份合成报告（一份 PDF、一份 CSV，写法不完全一样），三次读数被认成同一项，按日期排好，每个数字都标了出自哪个文件。
ChatGPT Health、阿福是厂商的云服务，注册就能用。Mirobody 是 Theta Health 开源的（Apache-2.0），国内的网页版和微信小程序也基于它。开源版能把记录和模型都留在自己电脑上，代价是得自己折腾，小模型也慢。它不做诊断，那次回答最后一句也是让我拿报告去问医生。

菲尔兹奖得主梅纳德谈“AI 攻克黎曼猜想”：相信证明正确，但成果被人理解、才可能得到认可
2022 年菲尔兹奖得主、牛津大学数学教授詹姆斯·梅纳德（James Maynard）在采访中表示，他认为 Anthropic 数学家莱文特·阿尔珀格（Levent Alpöge）与 Claude 合作完成的黎曼猜想证明是正确的，依据是该证明已通过 Lean 库形式化验证并经独立核实，且阿尔珀格过往有可靠记录。
菲尔兹奖得主梅纳德对 AI 辅助黎曼猜想证明的判断，提醒读者形式化验证通过不等于数学界认可，理解证明思想才是关键。
IT之家 11 月 22 日消息，当地时间 11 月 20 日，Anthropic 数学家莱文特 · 阿尔珀格（Levent Alpöge）宣布，自己与 AI 模型 Claude 合作，攻克了数学界最著名的难题之一 —— 黎曼猜想。
据IT之家此前报道，11 月 21 日，Lean 与 Mathlib 社区发布联合声明，以 Lean 库形式给出的黎曼猜想证明已经通过核验，该证明的代码约 1700 万行。
据每日经济新闻报道，2022 年菲尔兹奖得主、牛津大学数学教授詹姆斯 · 梅纳德（James Maynard）接受采访时表示，他认为这项证明是正确的，但强调“理解一个定理为什么成立，远比仅仅证明它成立重要”。 只有当有人真正理解这项成果，并能够向其他人解释清楚时，这份证明才有可能得到数学界的全面认可 。
梅纳德是当代解析数论领域的重要数学家，长期致力于素数分布等数学问题的研究。2022 年，他凭借相关研究成果获得菲尔兹奖。
由于这项结果已经获得形式化验证，而且这一验证又经过了独立核实。此外，阿尔珀格过去在提出此类重大主张方面有着可靠的记录。综合这两点，梅纳德称非常有信心认为这一结果是正确的。
梅纳德表示，虽然黎曼猜想确实有一些直接的数学推论，但这个问题之所以被认为如此重要，主要是因为人们一直期待，要解释素数分布中这种深刻的内在结构， 就必须发展出新的数学理论 。
在我们真正理解证明中的思想和整体框架之前，这项成果很可能无法带来人们所期待的变革。
不过，我相信随着时间推移，我们最终会真正理解这份证明，而这必将彻底改变我们对相关数学问题的认识。

items.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
items.description: How perplexity measures progress in AI models, and why it could help developers establish a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities.
items.excerpt:
By Jakub Pachocki, Chief Scientist at OpenAI
From afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities. There are indeed a variety of methods, but rather than designing something from scratch, they are mostly harnessing the intelligence coming from a much simpler and less interpretable process: training a compressor (or, equivalently ⁠ (opens in a new window) , predictor) on a very large corpus of data. 1
I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI. In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards. As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI. Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand, but that concern is outweighed by the urgency of establishing shared ⁠ (opens in a new window) safety measures across the industry. We at OpenAI hope for this to be a step towards building a shared scientific basis for future pacing efforts.
A simplified, but fundamentally informative, view of AI development is that first, one builds a large computer, then uses it to pretrain a model (compressor) on a large unstructured dataset, then applies a variety of techniques—like prompting, finetuning or reinforcement learning—in different contexts to elicit the latent capabilities of that model. Algorithmic progress can blur the distinction between training phases, but we can still separate the creation of the AI with hard-to-predict emergent capabilities (which I earlier dubbed “ an alien mind ⁠ ”) and the subsequent targeted elicitation.
The primary way we measure progress on this key “intelligence substrate” has remained remarkably constant over the years—we have been tracking the perplexity of the models on a held-out dataset. 2 , 3 Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions. The plot opening this blog post shows how this metric evolved for our models starting with GPT‑3.5.

items.description: OpenAI 撰文提议将 perplexity（交叉熵损失）确立为跨模型开发者比较和安全标准的共享指标，并公开其内部预训练测量数据。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/r7kb35fpdwc1m2iqsmd310tdj
items.excerpt:
OpenAI 撰文提议将 perplexity（交叉熵损失）确立为跨模型开发者比较和安全标准的共享指标，并公开其内部预训练测量数据。
OpenAI 公开自 GPT-3.5 以来的内部 log-perplexity 数据，并提出以困惑度作为跨实验室共享的安全限速指标。
从远处看，现代 AI 的构建方式似乎和过去几十年的软件差不多：用各种技术去实现特定的能力。方法确实五花八门，但它们大多不是从零开始设计，而是 利用 一个更简单、也更难解释的过程所产生的智能：在超大规模的数据语料上训练一个压缩器（或者 等价地说 ，一个预测器）。 1
我认为，跟踪训练更好压缩器的进展速度，是理解 AI 发展脉络的关键。在这篇文章里，我主张把困惑度（或等价的交叉熵损失）确立为一项指标，用来比较不同模型开发者之间的水平，并为共享的安全标准提供依据。作为第一步，我公开更多 OpenAI 在预训练方面的进展。公布我们内部的困惑度数据是经过一番考虑的：这会让竞争对手更清楚地看到我们的位置，但相比在整个行业建立 共享 安全措施的紧迫性，这种顾虑是次要的。OpenAI 希望这能成为迈向共同科学基础的一步，为未来的节奏把控工作提供支撑。
对 AI 开发有一种简化但本质上很有启发性的看法：先造一台大型计算机，用它在一个大规模无结构数据集上 预训练 一个模型（压缩器），然后在不同场景中运用提示、微调或强化学习等各种技术，把模型潜在的能力激发出来。算法进步会模糊训练各阶段之间的界限，但我们仍然可以把两件事分开：一是创造出具有难以预测的涌现能力的 AI（我此前称之为“ 异类心智 ”），二是随后有针对性地激发它的能力。
多年来，我们衡量这一关键“智能基底”进展的主要方式一直相当稳定——我们一直在跟踪模型在留出数据集上的 困惑度 。 2 、 3 困惑度衡量的是模型平均而言预测下一个 token 的能力；困惑度越低，预测越准。本文开头那张图展示了从 GPT‑3.5 开始，我们的模型在这一指标上的变化。
这一个指标所大致描述的模型能力范围令人惊叹。GPT‑2 在更早的数据集上刷新了困惑度的最优成绩 4 ，可以说它是第一个能够持续写出连贯段落的模型。下一次重大跃升是 GPT‑3，它具备了上下文学习能力，只要给出几个任务示例就能学会。GPT‑3.5 在我们当前主要评测数据集上的对数困惑度约为 0.99，能够进行流畅对话，也是初代 ChatGPT 的基础。GPT‑4 约为 0.91，擅长有效运用思维链推理，这也促成了后来对这一能力的有针对性激发，以及现代推理模型的诞生。如今，随着损失降到 0.8 以下，我们已经在网络安全和数学等领域看到了变革性能力的涌现。我想再次强调，事先完全无法确定 a priori 一旦达到这些精确的困惑度阈值，这些能力就会出现——它们从根本上可以看作是在这一个指标上取得进展所带来的涌现性潜在能力。
随着 AI 飞速发展，我们衡量下游能力的范围与方式可能很快就会变化。用大多数现代基准来评测 GPT‑2 和 GPT‑3 意义不大；而当年使用的基准在 GPT‑4 附近也基本饱和了。相比之下，我认为关注预训练进展很可能仍能提供有价值的信息。
进展速度的一个特殊变化，来自 AI 对自身发展的贡献越来越大。最常被讨论的指标，围绕 AI 在开发周期的各个阶段增强并取代人类研究员；最终的拐点被认为是“完全递归自我改进”，届时整个过程将完全自动化，不再需要人类监督。且不说出于维持人类控制的考虑，这种状态显然应当避免，我认为这种总体框架漏掉了关键的一点。开发过程中有一个关键环节可能带来潜在的阶跃式变化：预训练方面的算法研究。
我们最近在另一个领域见证了前所未有的加速。一年多来，我们一直把数学中的开放问题交给模型，作为评估它们的方式之一。当我们升级到对数困惑度约 0.76 的模型后，它开始产出突破性成果。对我们中许多曾在数学及相关领域工作过的人来说，看着我们长期思考的问题的解答在一个 Slack 帖子里接连从模型那里冒出来，感觉非常超现实。有了这样的经历，我们就可以外推——这种突然的转变在深度学习研究中同样可能发生。虽然这个领域更依赖实验，但历史上也有过简单的洞见被忽视多年的情况；因此最早到 2027 年，我们就有可能看到基础预训练进展出现类似的雪崩式突破 5 。虽然我预计 AI 也会对对齐与监控方面的进展做出重大贡献，但我认为这方面的进展不太可能快到足以让预训练释放出全部潜在加速。
新出现的惊人能力，主要来自压缩能力的进步，而困惑度正是衡量压缩的指标。因此，无论开发过程的自动化程度如何，困惑度都有望成为衡量通用智能的共享基准。从近期的进展外推，当我们进入约 0.68–0.7 的对数困惑度区间时，应当预期会出现进一步的变革性能力。我不知道这些能力会是什么，而且我们今天可能根本没有在测试它们。与此同时，我们也应当预期，目前占主导地位的对齐审计方式会 进一步退化 ⁠ ，模型对评估和训练的觉察也会进一步增强。我认为，前沿模型开发者应当共同努力，在模型首次投入使用之前，就如何评估这类模型、如何对其安全案例进行红队测试建立共同规范，包括共同的透明度标准。我还进一步提议，基于困惑度及其他测量指标设定 共同上限 ，开发者承诺在我们理解和监控 AI 行为的能力达到某个具体里程碑（例如开发出思维链监控器的后继者）之前不越过这一上限。也就是说，我希望形成一项行业标准：用某个可在各实验室间追踪的关键指标，规定开发的第一道上限，并明确在越过它之前我们需要具体达成什么。我希望这能引出一个共同框架，用来设定后续一道道上限，并为后续开发定下节奏。
跨实验室比较困难。 不同开发者使用不同的评估数据集，训练数据配比也各不相同。这里我们报告的是我们一直在追踪的主要数据集上的数字；我相信，只要确立透明度的目标，我们就能找到可迁移的方法来比较不同基础模型的质量。
与可操作的评估脱节。 困惑度并不直接对应我们关心的某项任务。关心它的理由在于，我们可以预期它上面的进步会催生出全新的能力。

items.excerpt:
The supply chain industry has invested heavily in detecting problems sooner. Transportation visibility systems identify late shipments, planning applications flag shortages, and control towers consolidate operational alerts. Yet knowing about an exception and resolving it are two different things. The delay may be visible to everyone, while responsibility for the next action remains surprisingly unclear.
That gap is becoming more important as artificial intelligence moves beyond answering questions and begins maintaining responsibility for work over time. On November 19, OpenAI expanded access to ChatGPT Dots , its persistent agents, to eligible ChatGPT Business Standard users, while testing access with a limited group of Plus subscribers. The agents can retain useful context, work with authorized applications, and pursue continuing assignments. This is not the same as releasing an autonomous transportation management system. It does, however, point toward an operating model that supply chain leaders should be examining.
The critical question is not whether an AI agent can produce a better recommendation. It is whether an organization can assign a bounded operational responsibility, know who is accountable for the result, and verify that the work was actually completed.
Consider how many logistics exceptions are managed today. A late container generates an alert. A transportation planner checks the revised estimated arrival, calls the carrier, and coordinates with a distribution center. Someone may approve a new receiving window or an inventory transfer. But the work does not end when the recommendation is accepted. The carrier must acknowledge the change, the appointment must be updated, and the revised plan must hold up as conditions change.
A great deal of operational effort is spent in the intervals between those actions. Employees chase confirmations, reconstruct previous conversations, and determine whether an apparent resolution was reflected in the system of record. Enterprise applications support the process, but they do not always maintain a single durable record of who owns the exception through closure.

items.excerpt:
Hours after Anthropic claims a Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, Stanford releases an all-human competing draft
Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 周五宣布与 Claude 合作得到黎曼猜想及广义黎曼猜想的证明，证明以 Lean 语言分 14 个数据包发布，打印将超 25 万页。
报道同时给出 AI 证明以 Lean 形式化验证和人类证明遭社区质疑两条线，读者可据此判断双方证明各自的验证路径与可信度。
Anthropic 的数学家 Levent Alpöge 周五表示，他用一个大语言模型解决了数学界最著名的未解难题。
据 Scientific American 等美国媒体报道，Alpöge 在自己的网站上发布了一篇论文和配套的计算机代码。他在 公告中写道 ：“我相信，在与 Claude 的合作下，我发现了黎曼猜想的证明。”
据 Alpöge 介绍，他的方法不仅解决了最初的素数问题，还一并解决了广义黎曼猜想（GRH）——该猜想把这一排序原理推广到一大类相关方程上。他预计，再给一点时间，他还能解决范围更广的扩展黎曼猜想。
从大学时代起，Alpöge 就把这个问题当作一个秘而不宣的终身目标，原以为要花上几十年。过去几个月里，他与 Anthropic 的 AI 模型紧密合作，负责把握方向，并在一个简化的玩具模型上把两种方法结合起来。等到转向真正的问题时，AI 接手了工作，在临近终点时把他远远甩在了后面。
为了攻克这道难题，两人扩展了数学家 Stepanov 的一个思路——后者曾在另一个数学体系中解决过类似问题。该方法依赖的工具类似于高中数学里对光滑曲线求导，而这一招用在整数上通常行不通，因为单个数值无法像连续曲线那样求导。
Alpöge 和 Claude 绕开了这个障碍：他们把特殊的数学变换像链条一样串联起来，模拟出求导的效果。关键洞见由语言模型给出——它发现，对于一个长度为 X 的数列，需要串联的变换数量恰好是 X 的平方根。Alpöge 说，单是这类想法就足以让同行数学家震惊。
Alpöge 公布消息几小时后，事情出现了戏剧性转折。就在一场董事会会议开始前，斯坦福大学数学教授、美国数学会（AMS）主席 Ravi Vakil 在博客上发布了一则 “紧急公告” ，分享了一份由数学家 Alessandro Masullo 独立撰写的广义黎曼猜想证明草稿。
“这完全出自人类之手，没有 AI 参与，”Vakil 写道。他说，斯坦福知名数论学家 Brian Conrad 已悄悄审阅 Masullo 的工作数月，提出了大量反馈意见，目前正被纳入修改。
Masullo 原本计划在斯坦福花一年时间完善草稿后再公开，但 Anthropic 突然发布的 AI 成果迫使研究人员立即公布了当前版本。
在首次发布公告约八小时后，Vakil 更新了帖子，称有数人联系他，报告了这份拟议证明中的问题，这些问题是在不同 AI 模型的协助下发现的。他说，尤其有几位数学家最先指出了这些问题。“按照惯例，在这份证明被承认为真之前，所有问题都需要解决到令学界满意的程度。（我对该证明策略的正确性不作任何断言。）”Vakil 写道。
数学家们之所以立刻认真对待这两项声明，是因为它们背后都有扎实的基础工作。Masullo 的传统证明经过了 Brian Conrad 数月的审查，而 Alpöge 则为他的 AI 证明提供了完整的计算机验证。
阿尔珀格说，如果把 Claude 的论证打印出来，篇幅会超过 25 万页，因为 AI 连基本规则都逐条写明，比如任何数要么大于二分之一、要么小于二分之一。为了免去数学家面对这堵文字墙的麻烦，阿尔珀格只以 Lean 编程语言的形式发布了证明，并拆分成 14 个数据包 。
Lean 就像一个数字裁判，逐步检查每一步逻辑推演是否都严格遵循数学的基本规则，没有错误，也没有未经证明的假设。据《科学美国人》报道，如果最初把原始问题翻译成代码时出了错，人为失误仍有可能发生，不过专家核查阿尔珀格对起始问题的编码是否正确应该不会花太久。瓦基尔则呼吁数学家尽快审阅马苏洛的草稿，将其翻译成 Lean 之类的系统，并补上任何细小的漏洞。
阿尔珀格承认，在某些复杂的子领域里，Claude 的水平远远超过了他，以至于他正在展示的成果，其周边的数学他还没有完全掌握。他预计这份庞大的 AI 证明可以很快被压缩，并计划在未来几个月内写出一个人类可读的版本。
Anthropic 的这则消息还赶上一个事关重大的商业周——就在周四公司 大规模 IPO 的第二天。阿尔珀格说，他是在周日深夜取得突破的，随后联系了 Anthropic CEO 达里奥·阿莫代伊请求批准发布。他称，时机恰好在公司上市之后，实在非常不幸，但他否认任何公关炒作的猜测，表示再等下去才真的不是选项。
这为进展飞快的 2026 年画上了一个句号——这一年里 Claude 已经解决了多个悬而未决的数学问题 。7 月，阿尔珀格发表了 Claude 生成的著名雅可比猜想解答。9 月，围绕描述流体和气体如何流动的纳维-斯托克斯方程，爆发了一场 激烈争议 ，起因是纽约大学数学家特里斯坦·巴克马斯特指出 OpenAI 使用了他和阿尔珀格的先前工作。10 月，OpenAI 在素数问题上迈出了重要的第一步， 发布了一批重要成果 。阿尔珀格明确称赞了 OpenAI 研究人员的选题，称这为他自己的证明提供了关键思路。
记者 约瑟夫·豪利特 在《科学美国人》的一篇详细分析中梳理了问题的核心。自伯恩哈德·黎曼于 1859 年提出这一假设以来，它一直是数论领域的北极星。大卫·希尔伯特将其列入 1900 年数学最重要问题清单，自 2000 年起，它作为克雷数学研究所七个“千禧年大奖难题”之一，悬赏 100 万美元。

November 20 2026 — the most famous problem in math is solved... revealing remarkable contrasts in human and AI approaches
Within a few hours of each other ( timeline ), two mathematicians claimed independent proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis, the most famous open problem in mathematics ( Scientific American ).
Levent Alpöge of Anthropic first made his Claude-driven proof in a note released with Lean code (1.3GB worth, ~250,000 page equivalent) rather than a full paper. Elliot Glazer confirms that the formalized statement is GRH and puts the chance of a Lean bug well under 1%. So if it finishes compiling with no extra axioms, it is probably correct, and no human will ever have read all of it…
…prompting Alessandro Masullo to release his 940 page, 100% human , work in progress proof he had been working on for the last 12 years (and had been undergoing secret manual review and revision per Kevin Hartnett ).
This is the third in the trilogy of frontier math breakthroughs, following from the Navier Stokes solutions and the Quasi-Riemann bounding, but it doesn’t feel over. OpenAI's September Navier-Stokes claim is still the cautionary tale: critics argued that its Lean proof did not match the natural-language result. Both AI-claimed Millennium Prize results will take years to verify.
Apart from the incredible accomplishment of the most famous problem in mathematics, one cannot miss the contrast that the AI-written solution is probably correct but incomprehensible , and the other solution is probably technically incorrect but understandable .
Open models are ready. Most coding harnesses aren’t. On DeepSWE, CodeAF finished #1 of ten on the same open model, ahead of Claude Code, at the lowest cost per fix.

Geodis’ Final Mile Cost Index reached 149.8 (2019 = 100), up 10.5% year over year and about three times the 3.5% rise in consumer prices, the company said in its inaugural “Final Mile Index.”
The measurement, which tracks quarterly U.S. delivery costs, performance trends, and risk factors, also reflected a record diesel price and second-quarter cargo theft losses that more than doubled.
GEODIS built the report around the three questions shippers serving the U.S. raise most once the invoice is understood: where freight is most exposed in the final mile, who answers when it goes missing or a truck crashes, and which controls actually reduce the exposure. Answering them gives shippers the visibility and accountability to deliver in the promised window, in full and intact, with a clear owner if something goes wrong.
"While pricing varies by customer, delivery service must always remain consistent, reliable, and accountable," said Kevvon Burdette, SVP, Business Development, Transportation, GEODIS. "Factors like cargo theft, chargebacks, and accidents threaten delivery certainty and raise costs. The Final Mile Index provides the benchmarks shippers need to spot risks, protect budgets, and build resilience."

items.excerpt:
Forecast of 182.7 million consumers would be down slightly from 2026 figure of 186.9 million shoppers.
An estimated 182.7 million consumers plan to shop during the Thanksgiving weekend this year, down slightly from 186.9 million shoppers last year, according to a report from the National Retail Federation (NRF).
Despite the dip, the figure continues the trend of elevated shopping during the holiday weekend seen in recent years. In addition, consumers continue to embrace earlier holiday shopping, with 60% starting by the beginning of November, up from 56% before the pandemic, according to results from the annual NRF survey, which was conducted by Prosper Insights & Analytics.
“Holiday shopping continues to be pulled forward, but Thanksgiving weekend remains an important shopping event for consumers,” NRF Vice President of Industry and Consumer Insights Allison Zeller said. “Shoppers are looking for deals, and retailers are delivering great value on gifts while creating special experiences that keep the Thanksgiving weekend shopping tradition going.”
Black Friday remains the most popular day to shop during the Thanksgiving weekend, with 69% (126 million) of holiday shoppers planning to shop. Of those, 67% are likely to shop in stores and 89% online. Cyber Monday follows in popularity, with 36% (66.1 million) planning to shop.
Throughout Thanksgiving weekend, 59% of holiday shoppers plan to use AI to support their winter holiday shopping. Top reasons for Thanksgiving weekend shoppers using AI include product recommendations (32%), brainstorming gift ideas (31%), gift lists and recipient tracking (25%), budget tracking (25%), and scanning retailer sites to find the best prices (25%).
“AI has become another tool consumers use to make holiday shopping easier, whether they’re researching products or looking for the best deals,” Prosper Insights & Analytics Executive Vice President of Strategy Phil Rist said. “As consumers incorporate these tools into their lives, holiday shopping represents one of the many ways they are putting AI to use.”
To keep their budgets in check this season, 82% are taking steps to manage holiday costs, including buying less expensive gifts (25%), cutting back in other areas (24%), buying for fewer people (20%) or waiting until Thanksgiving weekend to do most of their shopping (20%).

A four-company consortium of parcel giant FedEx and three investment firms has completed its previously announced $8.5 billion acquisition of InPost, a Polish provider of e-commerce parcel delivery services.
The specific investments made by each of the partners was not disclosed, but they had first announced the deal in February . The buyers included: the private equity firm Advent International, L.P.; the Czech investment group PPF Group; FedEx Corp. through its subsidiary FCWB LLC; and A&R Investments Ltd.—a financial entity founded by InPost CEO Rafał Brzoska. According to the new partners, that growth will be supported by structural sector tailwinds, including increasing e-commerce penetration, rising consumer demand for speed and convenience, and the shift towards more sustainable delivery solutions.
InPost says it is aiming to redefine the European e-commerce sector by improving the delivery experience for consumers and merchants alike, supported by the new ownership consortium’s accelerated investment in InPost’s digital offering and consumer experience, including its mobile app.

我们正在就一起安全事件通知客户。该事件涉及 2026 年 6 月和 7 月提交至 Together AI 无服务器推理服务的部分提示词。一个私有仓库的凭据在公开代码仓库中泄露后，未经授权的第三方下载了存储的提示词样本。

items.excerpt:
Together AI 宣布 阿里 旗舰模型 Qwen4 Max 上线其 Serverless 推理平台（模型串 Qwen/Qwen4-Max），1M token 上下文，截至 2026 年 11 月 22 日 7 折。
Together AI 用一次 65 万 token 的整仓修 bug 实测展示 Qwen4 Max 的长上下文编码能力，并给出价格、缓存和调用细节。
我们把一份 bug 报告和整个代码库一次性交给了 Qwen4 Max 。代码库是 Python Web 框架 Tornado：全部 344 个文件，652,519 个 token。模型没有工具可用，我们也没有预先挑选相关文件或先跑一遍检索。72 秒后它返回了一个补丁，而这个补丁通过了 Tornado 维护者为该 bug 编写的测试。这次请求花了 69 美分。
它还在仓库的其他地方找到了先例。bug 报告里从未提到 tornado/iostream.py ，但模型指出那里的代码已经用它的补丁所需的方式处理了错误。Tornado 维护者在自己修复时也引用了同一处代码。
Qwen4 Max 是阿里巴巴的旗舰 Qwen 模型。它今天已在 Together AI 上线，并在 2026 年 11 月 22 日前享受 30% 折扣。
Tornado 是一个开源 Python Web 框架。它的仓库包含约 340 个代码、测试和文档文件。这能放进 Qwen4 Max 的上下文窗口，而且远超任何人会手动粘贴进提示词的内容。我们挑选了维护者在 2026 年 11 月 18 日提交的一个修复——也就是 Qwen4 Max 发布两天后——并针对该提交之前的仓库状态进行了测试。
这个 bug 出在 Tornado 的 websocket 代码里。当连接关闭时仍有消息未发送，每一个未被 await 的 write_message() 调用都会记录一条错误，尽管 await 它是可选的。我们把该检出中的每个文本文件作为一个提示词发送，并附上一份只描述症状的 bug 报告：
当 websocket 连接在仍有消息未发送时关闭（例如，客户端发送了消息和一个 FIN，或重置了连接，却没有读取回复），每一个结果未被 await 的 write_message() 调用都会在 ERROR 级别记录“Task exception was never retrieved”。
await write_message 返回的 Future 是可选的，因此未 await 的调用不应记录任何内容。而确实 await 它的调用方仍应收到 WebSocketClosedError。
第一个 token 在 54 秒后到达，回复在 72 秒时完成。Qwen4 Max 将错误追溯到 tornado/websocket.py 中的 WebSocketProtocol13.write_message 。该方法把每次写入包装在一个任务中。当连接关闭时，任务因一个无人必须收集的异常而失败，Python 会将其记录为“Task exception was never retrieved”。
模型的补丁将该异常标记为已检索。这样就不会记录任何内容，而确实 await 写入的调用方仍会收到错误：
先例让这个补丁读起来像是项目本身的一部分。模型的解释称，修复应当做 BaseIOStream.write 已经为其自身的 future 所做的事。该方法位于 tornado/iostream.py 中，比 websocket 代码低一层，并且用同样的方式解决了同样的问题。维护者的提交也做了同样的比较。
没有人替它挑选这些文件。全部 344 个文件都放进去了，而模型找到了关键的那两个。
Tornado 维护者在修复中增加了两个回归测试：一个针对未 await 的写入，一个针对已 await 的写入。在修复前的代码上，第一个测试失败。应用模型的补丁后，两个测试都通过。随后我们在应用补丁的情况下运行了 Tornado 的完整测试套件，共 1,673 个测试，没有一个失败。
按折扣价计算，这次请求约为 69 美分，几乎全部花在 652,519 个输入 token 上。按原价计算则是 98 美分。
再次发送同一个仓库，费用会低得多。Together AI 会自动缓存提示词输入，促销期间缓存输入的价格是每百万 token \$0.0525。我们重复发送一个约 63 万 token 的请求时，几乎全部命中缓存。首个 token 8 秒就返回了，而不是 54 秒；输入费用约 3 美分，而不是 66 美分。
阿里巴巴于 2026 年 11 月 16 日发布 Qwen4 Max，称其为 Qwen 系列迄今能力最强的模型。该模型面向长时间运行的智能体任务，包括跨大型仓库的编码，这正是我们测试的那类任务。
Qwen4 Max 是一个稀疏混合专家模型，总参数 2.4 万亿，每个 token 激活 71 亿。在 Work360 上——这是阿里巴巴自建的基准，覆盖 721 个专业领域的行业任务——阿里报告称其整体表现优于 Qwen3.8 Max，在高推理强度下少用 35% 的 token，平均每个任务成本低约 60%。这些是阿里巴巴的数据， 其发布公告 中有详细说明。

items.title: The War Against Slop and an Emerging Weapon to Fight it: Formal Verification
items.description: Proving software correct with math has traditionally required specialist work. Now AI and Lean are helping automate the process.
items.excerpt:
Proving software correct with math has traditionally required specialist work. Now AI and Lean are helping automate the process.
The word of the year in the AI industry over 2026 has been “slop” — meaning low-quality output from a large language model. And with so much code being AI-generated now, avoiding slop has become a daily concern for software engineers. So how to do that? One way is to use formal verification systems , which use mathematical proofs and logic to verify the correctness of software or hardware.
With AI’s growing prowess at solving math problems , there’s now a number of AI companies offering formal verification systems. They include Harmonic , Theorem , Axiom Math , and a new entrant called &Truth (pronounced ‘and truth’). In this article we’ll look at some of the approaches these companies are taking.
In order to better understand the landscape of formal verification systems, we spoke to one of its leading proponents: Clark Barrett , &Truth’s co-founder and co-CEO. He’s also Corbel Professor (Research) of Computer Science at Stanford and was the co-creator of cvc5 , a popular automated reasoning engine used in formal verification.
Without getting too in the weeds, cvc5 is what’s called a “solver” for satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) , which Barrett says is widely used in companies like Amazon. For instance, cvc5 is used for specification analysis and test generation in Kiro , Amazon’s agentic development environment.
“It's been fun to see my tools go from a good idea in the lab to cvc5 is now called billions of times a day in production pipelines at Amazon,” Barrett told us.
Via a 2022 paper about cvc5 co-authored by Clark Barrett.
When AI coding agent companies talk about “verifying” their work, it typically means agents running tests, critiquing their own output, or having another AI model judge it. So I asked Barrett how far short of real verification does that fall?
“The main difference is really just, how do you know when you're done,” he replied. “So if you're testing, patching, scanning — using all these existing tools — they're quite good. 研究者在经过 OpenRouter 等 AI 路由的请求中埋入 200 万个金丝雀链接，测试敏感信息是否会沿 AI 服务链泄露，结果显示这些数据像筛子一样大量外泄。

研究人员在通过庞大 AI 服务网络发送的请求中埋下了 200 万个数字追踪标记，想弄清托付给这些服务的敏感信息究竟去了哪里。结果他们发现，这个生态系统泄露高度敏感数据简直像筛子一样。
这一暴露是通过一项巧妙的实验发现的，该实验旨在检验敏感信息是否会经由大量广泛使用的 AI 服务链条泄露，以及一旦泄露，这些信息又是如何被利用的。如今许多 AI 应用会使用 OpenRouter 或 Vercel 这类充当中间商的服务。这些“AI 路由器”（有时也叫“AI 网关”）接收 AI 应用终端用户发来的大量提示词，再根据最低收费、最适合当前任务等标准，把它们路由到可用的推理引擎。开发者不用 Anthropic、OpenAI 或其他大厂，而是雇一个 AI 路由器来寻找最合适的模型。

An analyst perspective on why orchestration, digital twins, and plant-floor integration matter more than the robot alone
Production logistics becomes a control problem
Rockwell Automation’s press conference presented a clear thesis: the next major productivity opportunity lies in the space between automated processes. Many factories have sophisticated machines and well-instrumented production lines, yet material still arrives through manual, disconnected workflows. The result is a familiar contradiction: a highly automated line can still depend on a forklift driver or an operator pushing a cart at its boundary.
“At the end of the line, there was a person driving a forklift and a person pushing a cart.”
That gap is where Rockwell is positioning production logistics. Rather than treating intralogistics as a stand-alone robotics project, the company describes an end-to-end workflow spanning production software, orchestration, controls, autonomous mobile robots, independent cart technology, and human work. This is a stronger industrial proposition than simply adding AMRs to a fleet. It treats the movement of work-in-process, components, packaging, and finished goods as part of the production system itself.
For manufacturers, the implication is significant. Material movement can become event-driven by production demand, quality status, inventory availability, and equipment conditions. The operational objective shifts from “dispatch a robot” to “maintain the production plan.”
Rockwell placed production logistics within a broader progression from connected operations to predictive and increasingly autonomous plants. Its “sense, think, act” framing is familiar in robotics, but the company extends the concept beyond the mobile robot to machines, lines, and plant-level workflows. Sensors establish context, software evaluates conditions, and physical assets execute the response, with a human retained in the loop where risk or uncertainty requires oversight.
“The right product to the right spot at the right time.”
This framing addresses one of the hardest problems in plant automation: local optimization does not automatically create system optimization. A packaging machine can be highly efficient while waiting for film. An assembly cell can meet its cycle time but starve because a component was not replenished in sequence. A warehouse can optimize picks while production priorities have already changed. The value of autonomy therefore depends on coordinating decisions

For decades, warehouse peak season was something operators could circle on a calendar. Black Friday arrived. Holiday orders surged. Distribution centers added temporary labor, opened extra shifts, increased transportation capacity, and prepared for several frantic weeks before volumes settled back into something resembling normal. That model is becoming considerably less reliable.
Promotions happen more frequently. E-commerce demand can change quickly. Product launches can create sudden volume spikes. Weather, geopolitical disruptions, tariffs, and viral products can alter demand patterns with little warning. For warehouse operators, the challenge is shifting from preparing for the peak to operating in an environment where a peak can appear almost anywhere. That change makes warehouse automation interesting for a reason that has relatively little to do with eliminating labor. The more important question may be: Can automation give a warehouse capacity exactly when it needs it?
DHL Supply Chain Offers an Interesting Test
A recent article from DHL Supply Chain provides a useful example. The company says it operates more than 9,000 collaborative robots globally , after adding roughly 1,000 units during the previous year. More interestingly, DHL says it can temporarily expand its active robot fleet by approximately 30 percent during peak periods . Its robotic systems have also supported more than 1.5 billion item picks . That 30 percent figure deserves attention.
Traditional warehouse automation economics have often been built around relatively stable throughput assumptions. A conveyor, sorter, or large AS/RS may produce tremendous productivity, but operators generally cannot add 30 percent more conveyor for November and remove it in January. Mobile robotics changes that calculation. If additional robots can be deployed temporarily, operators can begin treating automated capacity somewhat more like seasonal labor: bring it in when volumes rise, reduce it when demand falls. That is potentially a major change in warehouse economics.

Consider an AI transportation agent that identifies a delayed inbound shipment, determines that a customer order is at risk, evaluates alternative carriers, and books expedited transportation to protect the delivery commitment. From a service perspective, the decision may be entirely reasonable. From a financial perspective, however, the additional freight expense could eliminate the order’s profitability. The agent has successfully optimized one objective while potentially violating another.
This scenario illustrates an increasingly important distinction in the evolution of artificial intelligence: the ability to make a decision is not the same as the authority to execute it. As AI moves from providing recommendations to executing operational workflows, enterprises must establish controls that extend beyond the intelligence of the underlying models.
OpenAI’s new Deploying Daybreak Red reference architecture provides a useful framework for separating model capability from operational authority. The document concerns supervised cybersecurity investigations, not supply chain automation. Its relevance to logistics lies in the architecture of permission boundaries, isolated execution, independent monitoring, and the ability to stop an agent’s work.
Daybreak Red provides approved cybersecurity specialists access to advanced AI capabilities for authorized vulnerability research and supervised investigations. The reference design assumes a qualified human investigator, an AI coordination layer, an isolated execution environment, and target systems reachable only under defined rules. It should be read as a reference architecture for a particular controlled use case—not as proof that autonomous agents are safe to operate across live industrial or commercial networks.
The design separates the human investigator, the AI coordination environment, execution infrastructure, and investigated systems. Commands run within a restricted virtual-machine environment, and network permissions constrain which resources can be reached. Logging and supervision sit outside the agent’s own decision process. Crucially, the operator retains the ability to interrupt execution through controls the agent cannot override.

items.title: Ocean Freight Resilience Is a Network Design Problem, Not a Routing Exercise
items.description: Ocean freight resilience requires more than alternate routes. Learn how ports, inland transport, inventory and decision rights determine actual customer. The post Ocean Freight Resilience Is a Network Design Problem, Not a Routing Exercise appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The moment a major ocean corridor becomes unreliable, transportation teams look for substitute sailings. That can be necessary, but the ability to shift a vessel is not the same as the ability to continue serving customers. Effective resilience requires alternative ports, inventory positions, service commitments and cross-border processes to be designed before the disruption. In that sense, ocean risk is a capital-allocation and network-design question rather than simply a routing calculation.
A route is a sequence of transportation links. A network is the system of production sites, suppliers, inventories, ports, carriers, customs procedures, and customers that makes the route useful. A vessel diversion may add days or weeks, but the effects depend on what inventory is available elsewhere and which orders are most sensitive to delay. Two vendors in different countries may depend on one upstream component source. Two ocean services may share a transshipment hub. A customer may have several ports available but only one qualified distribution center. These common points of failure are rarely visible in a simple routing plan.
Suppose a manufacturer routes its inbound containers through a second port. The ocean service may be available, yet drayage capacity, customs brokerage, receiving labor and warehouse dock appointments could all be constrained. A different arrival location also changes inland distances, chassis needs and the inventory available to support customer orders. A scenario that merely substitutes a port code in the transportation system understates the work required to preserve service.
Risk-adjusted network design should compare the total cost of holding options open. That includes qualifying a secondary terminal, maintaining carrier and 3PL relationships, reserving strategically placed buffer inventory and documenting customs or inspection requirements. The cost of resilience is partly visible in premiums and working capital. Its value is visible in the orders that can still be fulfilled after the original plan fails. The correct unit of analysis is therefore a recoverable customer commitment, not an isolated container move.

items.title: MIT 数学面板讨论 AI 冲击下的数学研究未来
items.description: MIT 举办“AI 与社会：数学的未来”座谈，来自 MIT、哈佛、西北大学和纽约大学的数学家讨论 AI 对数学研究的影响。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/qfwgfsg8m1r4vcf4vglgi03by
items.excerpt:
Following the “mathocalypse,” mathematicians consider the future
MIT 举办“AI 与社会：数学的未来”座谈，来自 MIT、哈佛、西北大学和纽约大学的数学家讨论 AI 对数学研究的影响。
原文记录多位一线数学家对 AI 冲击数学研究的分歧观点，并给出期刊与人才培养正在调整的具体变化。
对数学界来说，这是动荡的一年。几十年来一直困扰数学家的一些重大开放问题，如今正被人工智能智能体在数小时内解决——企业会部署成千上万个这样的智能体，让它们不知疲倦、步调一致地攻克同一个问题。
AI 的迅猛崛起正在给这个领域带来关乎存亡的疑问：这些工具将如何影响人类对数学概念的理解？面对 AI 蛮力式的生产力，数学家还会有工作吗？而这一切对数学作为一项智识追求又意味着什么？
在麻省理工学院（MIT），数学家们在周一一场题为“AI 与社会：数学的未来”的小组讨论中，探讨了上述问题以及其他疑问。来自 MIT、哈佛大学、西北大学和纽约大学的顶尖数学家——各自都是所在领域的专家——坐下来进行了一场对话，话题涉及 AI 数学的质量、AI 如何挑战由来已久的研究规范，以及数学家不断演变的机会，无论他们是拥抱机器，还是坚持做“AI 纯素食者”。
这场内容广泛的讨论在 MIT 3 号楼一间座无虚席的阶梯教室举行，由科学作家、《代码中的证明》（The Proof in the Code）一书作者 Kevin Hartnett 主持，参与讨论的嘉宾包括：MIT 塞西尔与艾达·格林职业发展数学助理教授 Jacopo Borga；哈佛大学乔治·帕特南纯粹与应用数学教授 Michael Hopkins；西北大学萨拉·丽贝卡·罗兰数学教授 Bryna Kra；以及纽约大学柯朗数学科学研究所数学教授 Tristan Buckmaster。
“数学在过去两个月里的变化，比过去 100 年还要大，”Kra 说。她提醒道，AI 的力量将改变数学家的定义，也将改变以有意义的方式推进人类知识所需的条件。“这就像《双城记》开篇第一句：‘这是最好的时代，这是最坏的时代。’这是一个非常激动人心的时刻……同时也令人恐惧。”
过去十年，人工智能取得了稳步进展，这在很大程度上要归功于数学家自己——他们出于好奇，一直在打磨 AI 模型，让它们去解决已有已知答案的问题。这些早期练习被证明是成功的，最引人注目的是在 2025 年。那年夏天，在国际数学奥林匹克竞赛上，谷歌 DeepMind 的 AI 模型迅速解出了向全球最优秀的高中数学选手提出的大部分题目，达到金牌水平。
大约同一时期，其他数学家发现，一些 AI 系统能够解决已有已知答案的问题，但其解法相比人类数学家得出的解法略有改进。
2026 年，AI 的能力实现了飞跃。在若干案例中，科学家发现模型能够解决开放式研究问题——即没有已知答案的数学问题。随后在 9 月，OpenAI 发布了一项震动整个领域的公告：该公司将数千个 AI 智能体集中到一个单一挑战上，88 小时后，这些智能体给出了一个与纳维-斯托克斯方程相关的证明——这是千禧年大奖难题之一，也是七个无法解决的数学圣杯问题之一。
OpenAI 突然对纳维-斯托克斯挑战产生兴趣，恰逢小组成员之一 Tristan Buckmaster 的相关工作。经过一年的进展，他和他在竞争对手 AI 巨头 Anthropic 的合作者即将解决这个问题时，OpenAI 发布了公告。
OpenAI 抢先证明的冲刺引发了一场巨大争论：是否给予了适当的认可，数学家的数据是否被泄露，AI 智能体是如何得出解决方案的，该解决方案是否有任何实际意义，以及最重要的是，AI 将如何改变数学研究。
一个月后，该公司加倍投入，发布了 722 份手稿，按类别组织，涵盖了数学主题的方方面面。这些手稿声称完全使用 AI 解决了许多数学重大未解问题——这一成就被广泛称为“数学末日”。
但许多数学家坚持认为，问题不仅在于能否解决，还在于如何解决。他们说，当他们深入研究 AI 证明的细节时，并不清楚智能体是如何得出结论的。
“这些论文本身是无稽之谈，”Hopkins 在周一的讨论中说，并指出 AI 生成的证明包含“奇怪的想法”。他继续说：“仍然存在 AI 数学与人类数学的对立感。”
对于像 Kra 这样的数学家来说，数学史上的这一刻提供了一个机会，可以放弃某些长期持有的数学研究规范，例如研究小组之间的竞争以及第一个证明某个想法的声望，也称为优先权。
“你先做到并不重要，”Kra 说。“速度不应成为优先事项。这不再是关于证明的生产。我们需要找到其他方法来评估理解。”
然而，“我们可以抛弃优先权，但人们会想成为先驱，”Hopkins 反驳道，并指出数学家现在将面临的挑战，即在 AI 已经开辟清晰道路的领域取得进展。
“你可以以不同的方式成为先驱，例如在沟通[证明是如何产生的]方面，”Kra 说，他今年帮助起草了《莱顿人工智能与数学宣言》——一份由世界各地数学家签署的声明，呼吁采取行动应对 AI 对数学研究构成的风险。“数学的沟通现在更加重要。”
事实上，小组成员已经看到，从本科生到早期和资深职业数学家，各个层面对数学家的期望都发生了微妙的变化。
“面试变得越来越重要，”Kra 说，并指出仅仅根据数学家撰写或发表的想法来接受、雇用或提拔他们已经不够了——他们还必须证明自己理解这些想法并能向他人解释。
AI 还让数学家质疑学术期刊的作用，学术期刊长期以来一直是评估和验证数学进展的基准。
“我们评判[数学家]的百分之九十是通过期刊，”麻省理工学院的早期职业数学家 Jacopo Borga 说。“我不确定我们是否还应该这样做。我们应该提出一个新的衡量标准，并让它发展。”

Midterm elections have come and gone, but ‘twas the season for surveys, and this little report “The Great Unbundling” from Electric Twin on Gen Z caught my attention.
The premise of the report is that Zoomers are a little different—not that they are different from other generations (which is true, but not unusual), but that as a generation , they are configured differently such that “Gen Z” may not be that useful a term, at all. Rather than a single Gen Z with a relatively ascertainable bundle of preferences, there may be a multitude of Gen Zs, each one with less in-common with the other Gen Z “tribes” than you’d typically see for generations prior.
The reason for that fragmentation (so the theory goes) is social media: while previous generations rely on a “single source of truth” for their information mix (often with predictable partisan and geographic markers), Zoomers mix n’ match across different channels, forums and influencers. The result—and the contrast is most stark, when compared with Boomers—is a multitude of Gen Z cohorts that are better defined by their various online tribes than any particular country or political affiliation.
In other words, if you’re trying to understand what the Zoomers think, then you can’t look for binary left-right pairings vertically binned by country. Zoomer preferences come in a wider variety of bundles, driven more by their information mix, rather than politics or nationality.
With all that throat clearing, let’s dig in.
First, it should come as no surprise, but Zoomers get their content from very different sources than Boomers, especially:
Zoomers favor YouTube, Insta and TikTok, while Boomers are relatively heavy on Facebook.
The other thing to keep in mind is that short-form video’s arrival as an identity-making/sorting machine is fairly recent, roughly in-line with Gen Z’s maturation into adulthood. This data is actually from Pew, and not Electric Twin, but the implication is straightforward:

items.title: Five Warehouse Safety Upgrades to Plan Alongside Automation
items.description: From clearer aisle markings to stronger rack protection, five physical upgrades can make warehouses safer as they add robots and software.
items.excerpt:
Warehouse automation is trending — and rightfully so. Robotics and software systems solve many operational bottlenecks amid growing order volumes. They also mitigate the impact of chronic labor shortages .
Decision-makers should continue adopting digital technology . However, the shift to automation shouldn’t come at the expense of physical infrastructure . Here’s how prudent executives modernize tangible warehouse design elements for workplace safety and security .
The United States Occupational Safety and Health Administration requires appropriate markings on permanent aisles and passageways used by material handling equipment, such as forklifts. However, the agency doesn’t specify how wide the lines should be or what colors to use.
Following industry standards is a safe bet. For example, ANSI Z535.1 recommends orange for warning labels and yellow to communicate caution. This standard is a handy guide when color-coding aisles, traffic lanes, general walkways, equipment locations, inspection areas and other key zones across the warehouse floor.
Mounting parabolic or convex mirrors makes traffic paths, loading bays and personnel exit points safer. The curvature of these mirrors expands fields of view, which can help reduce blind spots and raise situational awareness among workers.
These safety mirrors come in different configurations. Generally, quarter or 90-degree domes suit sharp bends. Half or 180-degree mirrors fit T-intersections, while full or 360-degree domes increase visibility in cross aisles when suspended from the ceiling.
Commercial doors in warehouses and distribution centers have a demanding job. Busy loading environments require high-cycle door systems to withstand the rigors of heavy daily use. Industrial facilities often benefit from insulated sectional steel panels, which maintain consistent indoor temperature levels and protect inventory from dust and the elements.
Integrating a commercial door operator is key to streamlining loading and unloading operations. Models with sensors can detect obstructions and automatically reverse to prevent accidental closures.
These barriers absorb impact, helping keep racking posts intact when hit by forklifts, pallet jacks and transport vehicles. More warehouses have high clear heights to accommodate taller racks and support modern distribution.
Column barriers avert disaster, especially in facilities with autonomous mobile robots that can navigate independently across the floor

items.title: Nearly 3 in 4 Leaders Want People, Not AI, to Have the Final Say
items.description: A Körber survey of 2,000 U.S. and German leaders found that 76% say decisions have become more complex and 73% are uneasy giving technology the final say.
items.excerpt:
Artificial intelligence is playing a bigger role in business decisions, but most leaders still want a person to make the final call. In a new Körber repo rt , 73% of executives surveyed said they were uncomfortable letting technology have the final say.
Among U.S. respondents, 77% said AI was more involved in decisions, and 78% said decision-making had become more complex. Across the full survey, nearly three-quarters said too much data could make decisions harder or that decisions could stall while teams waited for information.
Körber released its AI and Decision Complexity Report on Nov. 18. Censuswide surveyed 2,000 senior leaders, split evenly between the U.S. and Germany, at organizations with more than $250 million in annual revenue and at least 250 employees.
Supply chain and distribution leaders reported the highest AI involvement in decisions, at 92%. Handling exceptions and dealing with variability were challenges for 36% of respondents, while 24% cited trouble getting systems to work together.
Healthcare and life sciences leaders reported slower AI adoption, at 60%. Their most frequently cited challenges were connecting systems (48%) and workforce skills (46%). Körber based each industry breakdown on responses from 50 U.S. executives.
About 59% of leaders at organizations making companywide changes planned to invest heavily in AI tools that help people make decisions. The share was nearly identical among organizations still in the pilot phase.
Leaders in the companywide group were more likely to say their organizations were performing well, at 64% compared with 42% in the pilot group.
“Most organizations are planning or executing significant AI-related investments, but spending alone won’t secure a return on investment ,” said Helena Garriga, a member of Körber’s executive board and president of its supply chain business.
Körber points to four things companies can put in place to get more out of their AI spending.

items.title: Rockwell Automation Agrees to Buy Austrian Mobile Robot Maker AGILOX
items.description: Rockwell Automation agreed to buy AGILOX from Carlyle, adding more driverless forklifts to its OTTO lineup and expanding its robotics business in Europe.
items.excerpt:
Rockwell Automation has agreed to buy AGILOX, an Austrian maker of driverless forklifts, from private equity firm Carlyle. Rockwell says the deal would more than double its autonomous mobile robot (AMR) business.
The companies announced the agreement on Wednesday. Carlyle took a majority stake in AGILOX in 2021.
Rockwell expects the deal to close in the quarter ending March 31, subject to regulatory approval and other closing conditions. AGILOX would join Rockwell’s Intelligent Devices segment.
The big draw for Rockwell is how AGILOX fits with OTTO, the AMR line it added when it bought Clearpath Robotics in 2023. AGILOX makes forklift robots that move pallets. OTTO is best known for its flatbed robots and already sells a driverless forklift. The deal would give Rockwell more models for moving pallets.
There’s a geographic fit too. OTTO is strongest in North America, while AGILOX has an established base in Europe. AGILOX also gets a door into Rockwell’s customers in consumer packaged goods and life sciences.
“Combining AGILOX and OTTO technologies creates a best-in-class technology platform,” said Blake Moret, Rockwell’s chairman and CEO.
He added that the deal “doesn’t just combine strengths; it amplifies innovation and delivers breakthrough value for our customers.”
Founded in 2017 and based in Neukirchen bei Lambach, Austria, AGILOX has deployed more than 2,500 AMRs for customers in automotive , third-party logistics , food and beverage , and pharmaceuticals . It has more than 250 employees and subsidiaries in Europe, the U.S. and China .
Carlyle says AGILOX has more than 400 customers worldwide and works with more than 40 partners across more than 35 countries. The firm also says AGILOX’s revenue has quadrupled since its 2021 investment.
AGILOX co-CEOs and co-founders Dirk Erlacher and David Niedermaier said the deal gives the company room to grow.

items.title: Descartes, Highway and Carrier411: The Technology Behind Freight Fraud Prevention
items.description: Freight fraud is an identity-continuity problem. Compare carrier monitoring, identity verification and dispatch controls across Descartes, Highway and. The post Descartes, Highway and Carrier411: The Technology Behind Freight Fraud Prevention appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Freight fraud has become a problem of identity continuity. A carrier can appear legitimate at onboarding, yet the person tendering a load, the dispatcher changing the appointment and the driver arriving at the dock may not belong to the same trusted chain. That is the operational question behind technology offered by Descartes, Highway and Carrier411: not how many checks a broker performs, but whether verified identity survives the move from contract to physical pickup.
Carrier vetting once relied heavily on operating authority, insurance certificates, safety records, and references. Those controls still matter, but a real motor carrier’s identity can be stolen. A fraudster may control a plausible email address, provide apparently valid identifiers, and represent a legitimate carrier whose dispatcher knows nothing about the load. An October 2026 Transport Topics examination described how companies including Descartes and Highway are connecting identity verification to tracking intelligence and carrier enrollment. Carrier411 contributes carrier monitoring and reporting tools. These are different functions, and no single database automatically proves possession of a truck or trailer.
There are several layers of exposure. Government operating-authority and safety records help establish whether a company exists and is authorized for a particular activity. Carrier-monitoring and incident-history systems help surface changes in risk. Identity-verification controls attempt to establish that the person and digital channel communicating about a load actually represent the carrier. Tracking, equipment and location information may expose an inconsistency after dispatch. These controls are complementary, not interchangeable: valid authority does not prove that an email, driver or trailer is authorized to collect a load.
The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration warns about broker and carrier identity theft and advises companies to check registration information and be alert to suspicious contact changes. Carrier411 describes its FreightGuard reporting framework as a source of reported carrier and broker performance issues. An ARC Advisory Group assessment of Descartes explains the opportunity to connect carrier, equipment, tracking and shipment data. The resulting systems should not be portrayed as interchangeable products, nor should the presence of a report automatically be treated as proof of wrongdoing.

items.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
items.description: OpenAI’s layered approach to adversarial distillation combines model training, safeguards, detection, and enforcement to protect against capability extraction.
items.excerpt:
How we’re addressing safety risks of distillation and lessons we’ve learned for strengthening safeguards across the industry.
As frontier AI models become more capable, safeguards play an increasingly important role in how they can be used responsibly. Adversarial distillation creates a path for bad actors to reproduce these capabilities without appropriate safeguards. An actor may use a frontier model’s outputs without authorization to train another model with similar capabilities, then deploy it without comparable protections. For instance, an adversary might distill a model’s cyber capabilities and use the resulting model to help carry out cyberattacks that the original model would have refused to assist with or that its safeguards would have blocked.
We’re sharing how OpenAI detects and disrupts adversarial distillation, how we’ve strengthened protections for our models’ protected reasoning, and what we’ve learned that can help strengthen defenses across the industry.
Our approach to adversarial distillation combines adversarial testing, model training, classifiers, and API-level protections with investigations into coordinated attempts to extract model capabilities. These updated safeguards align more closely with those we use for biology and cybersecurity.
We place particular emphasis on preventing attackers from extracting our models’ protected reasoning: the intermediate steps a model generates internally while working toward an answer, known as its chain-of-thought. These traces can contain information the final answer leaves out, making them especially valuable training data for another model.
W e’ve strengthened our defenses against protected reasoning extraction in GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol. In an internal adaptive evaluation using strong automated red-teaming , we tested whether attackers could recover protected reasoning the model had generated while answering an earlier prompt. The average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT‑6 Astra with its original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT‑6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards.
Distillation is a common machine-learning technique in which one model learns from data produced by another. items.description: Thinking Machines Lab 发布开源权重模型 Inkling 2 Mini，采用循环 Transformer 架构，将中间 12 层每 token 运行三次，总参数 26.4B、激活 3.4B，内存占用约 20GB，可在 32GB 内存以上的 Mac 本地运行。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/y7nk77dxae51qwi826gpmvbho
items.excerpt:
Thinking Machines Lab 发布开源权重模型 Inkling 2 Mini ，采用循环 Transformer 架构，将中间 12 层每 token 运行三次，总参数 26.4B、激活 3.4B，内存占用约 20GB，可在 32GB 内存以上的 Mac 本地运行。
原文给出循环架构设计、基准分数和可运行硬件门槛，读者可据此判断它是否适合本地部署和智能体任务。
今天我们发布 Inkling 2 Mini，这是一款速度快、能力强的模型，体积小到可以在你的笔记本电脑上运行。
Inkling 2 Mini 是一个循环式 transformer，每生成一个 token 都会把模型的中间层跑三遍。这样一来，模型能进行更多推理，用更少的 token 得出正确答案，在依赖推理质量的智能体编程等任务上尤其如此。在 DeepSWE v1.1（48.2%）和 Vals Index v2.2（46.5%）等基准上，Inkling 2 Mini 领先所有总参数量低于 100B 的开源权重模型，运行速度也比性能相近的模型更快。
DeepSWE v1.1。Ripple-65B（预览版）：44.3%，理论吞吐 4.7 tokens/s。Gemma 4 31B：0.3%，理论吞吐 10.0 tokens/s。Muse Glimmer：4.4%，理论吞吐 10.2 tokens/s。Qwen3.8-27B：42.2%，理论吞吐 11.4 tokens/s。Inkling 2 Mini：48.2%，理论吞吐 54.4 tokens/s。Gemma 4 26B A4B：0%，理论吞吐 80.8 tokens/s。Recursive Flint：10.81%，理论吞吐 122.8 tokens/s
SWE-bench Pro v2 Hard（51 项任务）。Ripple-65B（预览版）：79.1%，理论吞吐 4.7 tokens/s。Gemma 4 31B：14.2%，理论吞吐 10.0 tokens/s。Muse Glimmer：44.3%，理论吞吐 10.2 tokens/s。Qwen3.8-27B：73.8%，理论吞吐 11.4 tokens/s。Qwen3.6-27B：37.25%，理论吞吐 11.4 tokens/s。Inkling 2 Mini：77.9%，理论吞吐 54.4 tokens/s。Gemma 4 26B A4B：11.8%，理论吞吐 80.8 tokens/s。Qwen3.6-35B-A3B：28.1%，理论吞吐 102.3 tokens/s
Inkling 2 Mini 是一个混合专家（MoE）模型，总参数量 26.4B，激活参数 3.4B，考虑到循环，每个 token 的权重激活量为 5.4B。循环让模型能够推理更久，而不必把推理过程写下来，这对监控很重要：也就是我们通过阅读模型的思维链（CoT）来监督和理解其行为的能力。
我们用 Inkling 2 Mini 以及随它一同发布的一个研究专用的可变循环变体，测量了循环对性能和可监控性的影响。可变循环模型的无 CoT 时间跨度从单次运行的 16 秒提升到三次运行的 37 秒，其在一项串行推理基准上的表现一直提升到十次循环——是训练时循环次数的两倍。随着循环次数增加，模型的思维链变短了，但始终清晰可读。在智能体破坏行为的测试中，增加循环并没有让模型的得分呈上升趋势。
我们很高兴能为研究者提供首批采用循环架构的模型。可变循环模型被用于我们的可监控性实验，因为它能更清晰地在不同循环深度之间做比较。
Inkling 2 Mini 的大部分权重在训练和部署时都原生采用 NVFP4，最后四层为 MXFP8。Inkling 2 Mini 的总内存占用约为 20GB，因此可以在消费级笔记本电脑和桌面 AI 电脑等本地设备上运行。我们的研究人员带着 Inkling 2 Mini 上了一趟航班，它在 MacBook Pro 上离线运行，几分钟内就做出了一个可玩的飞行模拟器。
正在加载 Inkling 2 Mini 构建的飞行模拟器… 要试用飞行模拟器，请在桌面端打开此页面。
Inkling 2 Mini 以开放权重形式发布，今天已在 Tinker 上线，可用于推理和定制。
Inkling 2 Mini 的优势与 Inkling 2 Small 一致：它最擅长长周期智能体任务，在我们测过的大多数任务上，是同尺寸开放权重模型中的最佳。
在 DeepSWE v1.1、SWE-bench Pro v2 等智能体编程基准上，Inkling 2 Mini 的得分领先所有同类模型；在其他一些基准上则仅次于 Qwen3.8-27B。在内核优化基准 PMPP-Hard 上，它的成绩接近体量大得多的 Inkling 2 Small。
循环能提升模型的推理能力，但无法让权重存下更多事实——知识量主要取决于参数总量。在衡量事实性的 AA-Omniscience 上，Inkling 2 Mini 的得分与同尺寸的其他模型相当。研究 可变循环模型 时我们发现，长上下文基准的表现会随循环次数增加而提升，例如 GraphWalks BFS 和 MRCR v2；但知识密集型基准不会因循环次数增加而改善，例如 AA-Omniscience、SimpleQA Verified、SimpleVQA 和 WorldVQA。
Inkling 2 Mini 通过高效使用搜索和工具弥补了知识短板。在 BrowseComp、DeepSearchQA 和 MCP Atlas 上，它领先同尺寸的开放权重模型；在结合搜索与工具使用的知识工作基准上同样表现强劲。
